weakness.title: Missing Detection of Forced or Held-Open Openings
weakness.description: The facility does not detect when an opening is forced or held open, so the loss of its protection goes unnoticed.

extended_description.applicability: Doors, gates, hatches, windows and other openings that protect sensitive areas, including those controlled by an access system. An opening is held open when it stays open longer than a passage requires, whether propped, kept open by a defeated closer, or stuck by a fault. The detection required depends on the sensitivity of the area.
extended_description.exploitation: An unauthorized person uses an opening that has been forced or left open, because nothing reports its state.

row.details: A forced or open opening stays unnoticed, so the protection it provides is lost without warning.
The opening no longer restricts entry.

row.description: Fit openings to sensitive areas with position sensors that report whether they are open or closed.
Alert the personnel responsible when an opening is opened without a valid authorization, or stays open beyond a set time.
Use doors and gates that close by themselves when released, so that one left open does not stay open.
Adapt the allowed open time to the use of each opening, so that alerts stay meaningful.
Test opening sensors and their alerts periodically.
Fire doors may be held open only by approved devices that release on a fire alarm. Detection rules must account for them.

row.reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: PE-3 Physical Access Control, PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access
ISO/IEC 27001:2022, Annex A: 7.4 Physical security monitoring
